record.title: A paper reports that stronger next-turn metrics did not transfer to customer-support workflow success
record.summary: Laskar et al. compare gold-history next-action scoring with closed-loop execution on generated multi-turn customer-support workflows. Across Qwen3 4B/14B and Gemma 3 4B/12B, their paper reports that supervised fine-tuning increased average text-turn success by 25.2 percentage points, while tool-turn gains were smaller; the best fine-tuned model completed 8 of 77 tool workflows and no model passed the holistic workflow judge. The result is limited to the authors’ task generator, proprietary workflow dataset, and tested models; it does not establish that turn-level metrics are generally useless.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that supervised fine-tuning increased average text-turn success from 33.2% to 58.4% across four Qwen3 and Gemma 3 model sizes when each turn was evaluated with gold history.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report smaller average gains on tool turns than text turns; exact tool-call accuracy and argument matching remained low and regressed for some Gemma 3 settings.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In the paper’s table of 77 tool workflows, fine-tuned Qwen3-4B completed 3, Qwen3-14B completed 8, and neither Gemma 3 model completed any; the holistic judge marked 0 of 77 workflows successful for every model condition.

evidence_gaps.description: The reported differences have not been independently reproduced, and no public code or dataset artifact was located in the paper.

brief.importance_rationale: If the result generalizes, evaluation and training choices for tool-using agents would need to distinguish local action prediction from closed-loop task completion. Its consequence is meaningful for agent evaluation, while the evidence comes from one paper, a narrow customer-support regime, and unreplicated author-run experiments.
limitations: One author-reported study; no independent reproduction was performed in this activation.
The workflows are generated from a proprietary customer-support dataset, with GPT-5 agents simulating users and workflow agents and separate model judges filtering/evaluating conversations.
The held-out evaluation contains 84 conversations; the results table reports 77 tool workflows. Conclusions apply to this study’s task and evaluation setup.

Closed-loop execution uses deterministic parsing, a deterministic user simulator and up to two retries after an invalid tool call; other tool interfaces or recovery policies may produce different results.
A 0/77 holistic-judge score is not evidence that these models cannot succeed on other workflow types.

Across Qwen3 4B/14B and Gemma 3 4B/12B, their paper reports that supervised fine-tuning increased average text-turn success by 25.2 percentage points, while tool-turn gains were smaller; the best fine-tuned model completed 8 of 77 tool workflows and no model passed the holistic workflow judge. The result is limited to the authors’ task generator, proprietary workflow dataset, and tested models; it does not establish that turn-level metrics are generally useless.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report average text-turn success increased 25.2 points with SFT, tool-turn gains were smaller, and the best model completed 8/77 tool workflows; all model conditions scored 0/77 on holistic workflow judgment.
technical.demonstrated_result: The public preprint contains the described setup and reported table. The experiment was not rerun or independently reproduced here.
technical.mechanism: The paper contrasts per-turn predictions conditioned on gold histories with tool use and workflow replay conditioned on each model’s own prior outputs. The evaluation includes text similarity, LLM-judged turn success, exact tool-call checking, closed-loop replay and holistic workflow judgment.
technical.regime: Four fine-tuned Qwen3 and Gemma 3 models at 4B, 12B and 14B parameter sizes in 130 generated customer-support workflows; 84 held-out conversations and 77 tool workflows reported in the completion table.
technical.reproducibility: The paper describes its generated dataset and protocols but identifies no public code or dataset release; the workflow conversations originate from proprietary business conversations.
technical.strongest_baseline: Each fine-tuned model is compared with its corresponding zero-shot/base setting using the same paper-defined training and held-out workflow setup; no independent benchmark or matched external method was compared.

brief.title: A paper reports that stronger next-turn metrics did not transfer to customer-support workflow success
brief.why_it_matters: A model can become more likely to produce the expected next response without becoming more reliable at executing a multi-step task using its own prior outputs. If the reported pattern holds, tool-agent evaluation should report local action quality alongside closed-loop completion. The paper tests one customer-support setting and does not establish generality across workflow domains or agent architectures.
